# BACTERIAL MENINGITIS WITH L. MONOCYTOGENES

Once a diagnosis of acute bacterial meningitis is considered likely,
antimicrobials should be initiated as soon as possible. Two blood cultures
should be drawn. Lumbar puncture (LP) should be performed in nearly all patients
to obtain cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) for establishing diagnosis and determining
infectious organism/susceptibility. Adjust antimicrobial regimen to optimize
therapy and treatment duration based on pathogen once isolated.

# Consult Infectious Diseases

# Duration of Therapy

Treat for a total duration of 21 days. If gentamicin is added for synergy, treat
for at least 1 week. May be extended for up to 3 weeks in those who are poor
responders and do not have signs of toxicity.

# Treatment

Preferred:

[Ampicillin 2 gm IV q4h \($$\) R for 21 days](psjizid-ampicillin-2-gm-iv-q4h)

< OPTIONAL ADD ON TO ONE OF THE AGENTS ABOVE FOR SYNERGY >
[Gentamicin 2 mg/kg IV x 1 then 1.7 mg/kg IV q8h \($\) R,O for 7 days](psjizid-gent-2mg-kg-iv-once-then-1-7mg-kg-iv-q8h)

Alternative:

[Assessment of beta-lactam reaction](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Trimethoprim 5 mg/kg - sulfamethoxazole 25 mg/kg IV q6h \($$$\) R,DI](psjizid-trimeth-sulfa-5-25-mg-kg-iv-q6h)
